lots.what_it_is: Edwardian-style stained hardwood pot cupboard with green Art Nouveau tile splashback (two yellow flower tiles), single panelled door, two internal shelves, plus two green enamel chamber pots. Paper label inside reads COOGAN'S TASMANIA with Job, Design and Bench numbers handwritten.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The only entry (Smith & Singer) was opened and dropped as a different, much earlier and more valuable item.
lots.working: No surviving SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are both 0. All-in cost would be hammer x 1.22, pickup only.
lots.confidence_reason: Label read clearly in photo 3, but no comparable price evidence of any kind survives.
lots.dropped_entries: Smith & Singer KEITHOKEY lot 186 (page opened by curl): verified as 'An Australian cedar bedside pot cupboard, circa 1840', estimate $1,000-1,500, Lot Sold $2,400 hammer ($2,880 with premium). Price is real but it is a colonial cedar piece, not a factory-made Edwardian tiled-back cupboard, so it is not the same item and was dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: paper label 'COOGAN'S TASMANIA' with Job No., Design No., Bench No., Dept and Exd. by filled in by hand, label intact with light staining. Photos 1, 2 and 4: tiled splashback with two floral tiles intact, top with some finish wear and small marks, door with original-looking latch, interior shelves plain. Enamel pots show chips to rims and handles.
lots.condition: Good used condition from photos: finish wear to top, tiles appear intact, label intact. Enamel chamber pots chipped.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are all splashback tiles intact without cracks, and is the door latch working?
lots.score_reason: Modest Tasmanian-labelled Edwardian-style bedside cupboard; likely worth roughly $50-150 locally, but no price evidence found.

lots.what_it_is: Two-box mixed lot: Japanese eggshell and Satsuma-style plates and cups (one with a geisha lithophane-style picture), modern Chinese laughing Buddha with children, blue and white jugs, pressed glass lidded bowl, candlesticks, small lidded pot, and a turquoise and grey drip-glaze jug, small jug and wavy basin set in the Ditmar Urbach style (no mark seen).
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. Both entries dropped as not the same item.
lots.working: No surviving SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark visible on the drip-glaze jug and basin, so the Ditmar Urbach attribution is unconfirmed; no surviving comps.
lots.dropped_entries: (1) eBay ebay.de/itm/305422503297, US$60 asking, Ditmar Urbach vase: eBay is closed to us, snippet only, and a single vase is not this jug and basin set, so dropped. (2) Rago Nov 2023 lot 187 (page opened by curl): actually titled 'Erphila, Collection of seven works', six bird pitchers and a mug, largest stamped Ditmar Urbach; result US$1,386 is including premium (result without premium US$1,100), estimate US$1,500-2,000. Marked figural pieces from the Kovel collection, not comparable to an unmarked jug and basin, so dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: drip glaze jug, small jug and basin, no base shown so no maker's mark read. Photo 2: Japanese eggshell plates and cups, some with visible wear; laughing Buddha appears modern. Photo 1: blue jug, blue and white jug, pressed glass lidded bowl, candlesticks.
lots.condition: Mixed; some plates chipped or cracked per researcher, drip-glaze set looks intact in photo but underside not seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a maker's mark (e.g. Ditmar Urbach, Czechoslovakia) on the base of the turquoise drip-glaze jug or basin, and are they free of chips or cracks?
lots.score_reason: Ordinary box lot; realistic value about $30-60 even allowing for the drip-glaze set, which is unmarked in the photos.

lots.what_it_is: Four framed pieces. The only one with a market is a hand-coloured steel-engraved Tallis/Rapkin map of Tasmania ('Van Diemen's Island or Tasmania', London Printing and Publishing Co, c.1851-54 state with the seal at left and vignettes), window-mounted with a red mat under glass in a wooden frame, toned and foxed. Also: unsigned gatehouse watercolour/gouache in a gilt frame, small unsigned lake and mountain oil in an ornate gilt frame, and a sepia etching of a building facade in a dark frame.

sold.note: Page opened (curl). 'Van Diemen's Island or Tasmania', condition A, minor offsetting and a hint of toning along centrefold, unframed. Sold below estimate. 12 years old. Rate USD 1 = AUD 1.425 (open.er-api.com, 29 Sep 2026), today's rate not the 2014 rate.
Page opened (curl). Earlier state, condition A, fine original outline colouring, borders and vignettes uncoloured as issued, unframed. Very old sale. Rate USD 1 = AUD 1.425.
Page opened (curl). Condition A, good impression and colour, close margin at one side just nicking border, unframed. Very old sale. Rate USD 1 = AUD 1.425.

asking.note: Page opened (curl). 'C1854 Van Diemen's Island or Tasmania', John Tallis, fourth state with the seal at left, in stock, A$395. Researcher had this as GBP 140-155, which was wrong; corrected. Dealer retail for an unframed sheet, well above auction level and above what a foxed framed copy would make.

lots.guide_summary: 3 sold, 0 unsold, 1 asking. Sold prices run A$114-214 (USD 80-150, all 2002-2014, unframed, better condition than this foxed copy); the single dealer asking price of A$395 is well above sold. USD converted at 1.425 (live, 29 Sep 2026). The three other framed pictures add little.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD = USD 80 = A$114 (2002). 114 / 1.22 = 93.4, rounded down to $90 hammer, all-in $109.80. Flip: likely resale taken as A$157 (middle of the three SOLD prices; this copy is foxed so not higher). Less eBay-type selling fee about 13% (A$20) and outbound postage about A$20 for a framed item = A$117. 117 / 2.44 = 47.9, rounded down to $45 hammer, all-in $54.90. Pickup only, inbound freight $0. The SOLD evidence is old and overseas, so treat these as ceilings.
lots.confidence_reason: Tallis Tasmania layout, border, vignettes, seal and HOBART lettering visible, but the title cartouche is not legible in the photos. Two same-item SOLD entries plus one close, all page-opened, but all 12-24 years old and for unframed copies in better condition.
lots.dropped_entries: (1) Classical Images URL returned HTTP 404 by curl, no price seen; dropped. (2) Bartele Gallery page opened: shows 'Price on request', no EUR 230 price anywhere, so dropped. (3) The Unique Maps / Geographicus GBP figures were not re-verified (Geographicus closed with a 403 security check earlier); the Antique Print Map Room URL was opened and its real price (A$395) kept instead.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 and enlarged crops: hand-coloured steel engraving of Tasmania with HOBART legible, coloured district boundaries, decorative Tallis border and vignette views, round seal at left indicating the c.1851-54 state. Paper toned with foxing spots. Photo 1 crop: red window mat, gilt slip, wooden frame with a small chip on the lower left edge. Other three works show no legible signatures.
lots.condition: Map toned and foxed, framed under glass so margins and reverse not seen; frame has minor knocks. Other three pieces fair decorative condition.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can the map be checked out of the frame for trimming, tears, heavy foxing or water staining, and is it an original engraving rather than a later reproduction print?
lots.score_reason: A genuine framed Tallis Tasmania map is worth roughly A$100-250 at auction; foxing and old evidence pull it to the lower end, and the three decorator pieces add perhaps A$20-60.
